issues.legal_issue: A suit brought on behalf of an idol to establish its title to property and recover possession from an unlawful possessor falls outside the scope of the restrictions governing public religious or charitable trust suits.
material_facts: The suit was brought on behalf of the idol seeking a declaration of its title to property and possession from the purchaser under an alienation made by the temple manager.
The courts below found that the alienation was not for the idol’s benefit and that its consideration was inadequate.
issues.conclusion: The suit was outside the scope of section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure and was not barred by that section.
issues.legal_principle: Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure applies only where the trust is created for public charitable or religious purposes, there is a breach of trust or a need for the court’s direction in administering it, and the relief sought is one of those enumerated in the section. A suit by an idol to declare its title and recover possession from a person in possession under a void alienation enforces the idol’s private right and seeks relief not enumerated in section 92. The Court relied on Abdur Rahim v. Barkat Ali and Mahant Pragdasji Guru Bhagwandasji v. Patel Ishwarlalbhai Narsibhai, and referred to Mukhda Mannudas Bairagi v. Chagan Kisan Bhawasar, Darshan Lal v. Shibji Maharaj Birajman, and Madhavrao Anandrao Raste v. Shri Omkareshvar Ghat.

predicates.idol_property_recovery_suit: A proceeding is brought on behalf of an idol to recover property claimed as belonging to it.
predicates.seeks_title_declaration_and_possession: The proceeding seeks a declaration of the idol’s title and possession of the property from its possessor.

issues.definition: When a proceeding on behalf of an idol seeks both a declaration of its title and recovery of its property, the rule is that it is not barred by public-trust-suit restrictions.

issues.legal_issue: A worshipper may represent an idol in a suit to protect its property when the person ordinarily entitled to represent it acts adversely to its interests or fails to protect them.
material_facts: The temple manager alienated the idol’s property and did not take steps to recover it.
The suit was brought on behalf of the idol by a worshipper who was interested in its worship and had assisted in managing the temple.
The suit sought to protect the idol’s interests and recover its property.
issues.conclusion: In the circumstances, the worshipper could represent the idol, and the suit was maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: An idol is a juridical person and ordinarily acts through its Shebait, who is generally entitled to bring suits to protect its property. But where the Shebait acts adversely to the idol’s interests or leaves them unprotected, a person interested in the idol’s worship may receive an ad hoc power to represent it and protect its interests. The Court relied on Pramatha Nath Mullick v. Pradyumna Kumar Mullick and Kanhaiya Lal v. Hamid Ali, and referred to Kalyana Venkataramana Ayyangar v. Kasturi Ranga Ayyangar and Maharaja Jagadindra Nath Roy Bahadur v. Rani Hemanta Kumari Debi. It disapproved Kunj Behari Chandra v. Sri Sri Shyam Chand Thakur and Artatran Akkhagadi Brahma v. Sudersan Mohapatra.

rule.if: idol_property_protection_suit and interested_worshipper and (representative_acted_adversely or representative_failed_to_protect)

predicates.idol_property_protection_suit: A proceeding is brought on behalf of an idol to protect its interests in property.
predicates.interested_worshipper: A person interested in the idol’s worship brings the proceeding on its behalf.
predicates.representative_acted_adversely: The person ordinarily representing the idol acted against its interests.
predicates.representative_failed_to_protect: The person ordinarily representing the idol failed to take steps to protect its interests.

issues.definition: If a person interested in an idol’s worship brings a property-protection proceeding for it and its ordinary representative either acted against its interests or failed to protect them, the rule permits that worshipper to represent the idol.
